textSets.title: Updated delivery schedule
textSets.passage:
From: Elena Ortiz, Facilities Coordinator
To: All department assistants
Subject: Office chair delivery

The new ergonomic chairs were originally scheduled to arrive on Tuesday. The supplier has informed us that heavy traffic at the regional warehouse has [131] the shipment by one day. The delivery crew will now arrive Wednesday between 9:00 A.M. and noon. [132], each department should keep the hallway outside its work area clear during that period.

Before the crew arrives, please [133] the labels on your department's existing chairs. The labels indicate which chairs should be removed and which should remain in place. [134]

If Wednesday creates a serious scheduling conflict for your team, contact me by 3:00 P.M. today. I will coordinate a separate delivery time with the supplier.

questions.correctExplanation: The present perfect construction 'has delayed' requires the past participle and describes a change with a present consequence.

distractorExplanations.B: The base form cannot follow 'has' in this present perfect construction.
distractorExplanations.C: The -ing form would require 'has been' and would change the structure.
distractorExplanations.D: The third-person present form cannot follow the auxiliary verb 'has'.

questions.completedContext: The supplier has informed us that heavy traffic at the regional warehouse has delayed the shipment by one day.
questions.extraExample: The carrier has postponed the morning pickup.

questions.correctExplanation: The need to clear the hallway is a practical consequence of the delivery crew's revised arrival, so a result connector is required.

distractorExplanations.A: 'Nevertheless' signals contrast, but the instruction follows logically from the delivery plan.
distractorExplanations.B: The hallway instruction is not an example of the arrival time; it is a consequence.
distractorExplanations.C: 'Meanwhile' emphasizes simultaneous events, not the cause-and-result relationship here.

questions.completedContext: The delivery crew will now arrive Wednesday between 9:00 A.M. and noon. Therefore, each department should keep the hallway clear.
questions.extraExample: The entrance will be busy; therefore, use the side door.

questions.correctExplanation: In this workplace context, 'verify the labels' naturally means to check that the identification labels are correct before collection.

distractorExplanations.A: 'Recover the labels' would mean getting them back, which is not the requested preparation.
distractorExplanations.C: 'Persuade' requires a person or group as its object, not identification labels.
distractorExplanations.D: 'Celebrate the labels' is grammatically possible but has no sensible workplace meaning.

questions.completedContext: Before the crew arrives, please verify the labels on your department's existing chairs.
questions.extraExample: Please verify the address before submitting the order.

choices.text: Most employees ordered lunch from a nearby café.
The warehouse opened a second branch last year.
This will help the crew complete the replacement efficiently.
A different supplier sells desks in several colors.

questions.correctExplanation: 'This' refers to labeling the chairs, and the sentence explains how that preparation helps the delivery crew before the email moves to scheduling conflicts.

distractorExplanations.A: The lunch detail is unrelated to chair labeling or delivery preparation.
distractorExplanations.B: A warehouse expansion does not refer back to the requested labeling action.
distractorExplanations.D: Desk colors introduce an unrelated supplier and break the email's delivery sequence.

questions.completedContext: The labels indicate which chairs should be removed and which should remain in place. This will help the crew complete the replacement efficiently.
questions.extraExample: Mark each box clearly. This will help us sort the shipment.

textSets.title: Community workshop registration
textSets.passage:
RIVERSIDE COMMUNITY CENTER
Weekend Photography Workshop

Registration is now open for our introductory photography workshop on Saturday, October 17. The class is designed for adults who want to take better photographs with a phone or a basic digital camera. No previous experience is [135]. Instructor Maya Chen will demonstrate simple techniques for lighting, framing, and outdoor portraits.

The fee is $25 and includes printed materials. Participants should bring their own device and arrive fifteen minutes early [136] staff can confirm registrations before the 10:00 A.M. start. [137]

Space is limited to eighteen people. To reserve a place, complete the online form and submit payment by October 12. Registrations received after that date will be accepted only if seats remain [138].

questions.correctExplanation: The notice describes an introductory class, so 'No previous experience is required' clearly states that experience is not a condition for joining.

distractorExplanations.B: Experience cannot logically be repaired in the context of course admission.
distractorExplanations.C: Experience is gained or required, not delivered to a participant.
distractorExplanations.D: 'Compared' would need another item of comparison and does not state an admission condition.

questions.extraExample: No special equipment is required for the tour.

questions.correctExplanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of arriving early: giving staff enough time to confirm registrations before the class begins.

distractorExplanations.A: 'Although' introduces contrast, but the two actions have a purpose relationship.
distractorExplanations.C: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition that is not present in this instruction.
distractorExplanations.D: 'Despite' must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund, not this full clause.

questions.completedContext: Participants should arrive fifteen minutes early so that staff can confirm registrations.
questions.extraExample: Please sign in early so that we can start on time.

choices.text: The center's gymnasium was renovated in May.
Several professional cameras are displayed in the lobby.
A short outdoor practice session will follow the indoor demonstration.
Workshop fees increased for advanced courses last winter.

questions.correctExplanation: The sentence extends the description of workshop activities and explains why participants need their own device, while maintaining the event's chronological sequence.

distractorExplanations.A: A gym renovation is unrelated to the photography workshop schedule.
distractorExplanations.B: A lobby display does not develop the instructions or workshop sequence.
distractorExplanations.D: Past pricing for other courses interrupts the current workshop information.

questions.completedContext: Participants should bring their own device. A short outdoor practice session will follow the indoor demonstration.
questions.extraExample: A guided practice activity will follow the presentation.

questions.correctExplanation: After the linking verb 'remain,' an adjective is needed to describe the condition of the seats, making 'available' the correct form.

distractorExplanations.B: The noun 'availability' cannot directly complement 'seats remain' in this structure.
distractorExplanations.C: The adverb form does not describe the noun 'seats' after the linking verb.
distractorExplanations.D: The verb 'avail' cannot serve as the adjective complement required here.

questions.completedContext: Registrations received after that date will be accepted only if seats remain available.
questions.extraExample: A few appointments remain available this week.

textSets.title: Mobile banking maintenance
textSets.passage:
NORTHLINE BANK SERVICE UPDATE

We will perform scheduled maintenance on the Northline mobile banking application from 1:00 A.M. to 4:30 A.M. this Sunday. During this period, customers will be [139] to view recent transactions, but transfers and mobile check deposits will be temporarily unavailable. Online banking through our website will continue to operate normally.

Customers who need to schedule a transfer are [140] to do so before maintenance begins. [141] The update will improve sign-in reliability and add clearer notifications when a transaction requires additional review.

We expect all mobile services to return by 4:30 A.M. [142], if work takes longer than planned, current information will be posted on the Service Status page. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your patience.

questions.correctExplanation: The fixed structure 'will be able to' expresses continued capability during maintenance and requires the adjective 'able.'

distractorExplanations.A: The noun 'ability' would require a different structure such as 'have the ability.'
distractorExplanations.C: The verb 'enable' would require an object indicating who gains the capability.
distractorExplanations.D: The adverb 'ably' cannot complete the phrase 'will be ... to view.'

questions.completedContext: During this period, customers will be able to view recent transactions.
questions.extraExample: Members will be able to access their statements online.

questions.correctExplanation: The service notice naturally uses the formal collocation 'customers are advised to' when recommending an action before temporary maintenance.

distractorExplanations.A: 'Produced to' does not express guidance or a recommended action.
distractorExplanations.B: 'Discovered to' does not form a grammatical recommendation structure.
distractorExplanations.C: Customers cannot be 'borrowed to' perform an action in this context.

questions.completedContext: Customers who need to schedule a transfer are advised to do so before maintenance begins.
questions.extraExample: Travelers are advised to arrive two hours early.

choices.text: The bank's first branch opened near Central Station.
No action is needed to install the updated version of the application.
Printed checks are available in several background colors.
The website recently published an interview with a local artist.

questions.correctExplanation: The sentence answers a likely customer concern about the maintenance update, and 'the updated version' connects directly to the following description of improvements.

distractorExplanations.A: The history of a branch does not connect to app maintenance or the following update.
distractorExplanations.C: Check designs are unrelated to installation and mobile-service improvements.
distractorExplanations.D: An artist interview has no logical relationship with the application's update.

questions.completedContext: No action is needed to install the updated version of the application. The update will improve sign-in reliability.
questions.extraExample: No action is required; the update will install automatically.

questions.correctExplanation: The notice contrasts the expected completion time with the possibility of a delay, so the contrast connector 'However' is appropriate.

distractorExplanations.A: The possibility of delay is not an example of the expected completion time.
distractorExplanations.B: The second idea is a qualification, not a similar parallel situation.
distractorExplanations.D: A possible delay is not a result caused by the expected completion time.

questions.completedContext: We expect all mobile services to return by 4:30 A.M. However, if work takes longer, information will be posted online.
questions.extraExample: The office should open at nine. However, check the website for delays.

textSets.title: A quieter lunch program
textSets.passage:
A QUIETER LUNCH PROGRAM SHOWS EARLY RESULTS

Three months ago, Marston Design introduced optional quiet tables in its employee cafeteria. The tables were created for people who wanted a short break from conversation during the workday. At first, managers were [143] that the idea might make the cafeteria feel less welcoming. Employee surveys, however, have shown the opposite.

Nearly sixty percent of respondents said they had used a quiet table at least once, and most described the experience [144]. [145] The company has since added two more quiet tables while preserving the larger shared seating area for group lunches.

The program's organizers emphasize that the tables are not intended to discourage conversation. [146], they give employees another way to use their lunch period according to their needs. Marston plans to review the program again at the end of the year.

questions.correctExplanation: The clause after the blank describes a possible negative effect, so 'concerned that' accurately expresses the managers' initial worry.

distractorExplanations.A: 'Arranged that' suggests planning an event and does not express the stated uncertainty.
distractorExplanations.B: 'Celebrated that' would express approval, which conflicts with the feared negative effect.
distractorExplanations.D: 'Measured that' is not a natural verb pattern for introducing this concern.

questions.completedContext: At first, managers were concerned that the idea might make the cafeteria feel less welcoming.
questions.extraExample: Residents were concerned that construction would increase traffic.

questions.correctExplanation: The adverb 'favorably' modifies the verb 'described' and indicates that employees spoke positively about the experience.

distractorExplanations.A: The noun or verb 'favor' cannot modify how respondents described the experience.
distractorExplanations.B: 'Favorite' identifies a preferred item and does not function as the required adverb.
distractorExplanations.C: The adjective 'favorable' would need to modify a noun rather than the verb 'described.'

questions.completedContext: Most respondents described the experience favorably.
questions.extraExample: Participants responded favorably to the proposal.

choices.text: Several noted that a few quiet minutes helped them return to work feeling more focused.
The design company moved into its current building twelve years ago.
Cafeteria prices are reviewed by an outside supplier every spring.
Managers usually hold weekly meetings on another floor.

questions.correctExplanation: 'Several' refers to survey respondents, and their comments provide evidence for the favorable survey result before the article describes the program's expansion.

distractorExplanations.B: The building's history does not explain employee survey responses or the expansion.
distractorExplanations.C: Price reviews are unrelated to the reported benefit of quiet seating.
distractorExplanations.D: Meeting location does not provide evidence about the lunch program's results.

questions.completedContext: Most described the experience favorably. Several noted that a few quiet minutes helped them return to work feeling more focused.
questions.usefulPattern: survey result → respondent evidence → program decision
questions.extraExample: Many rated the service highly. Several specifically praised its speed.

questions.correctExplanation: 'Instead' corrects a possible misunderstanding: the tables do not discourage conversation; they offer an additional choice for lunch breaks.

distractorExplanations.B: 'Otherwise' introduces a consequence if a condition is not met, which is absent here.
distractorExplanations.C: The second sentence is a reformulation of purpose, not an example of discouraging conversation.
distractorExplanations.D: 'Meanwhile' marks simultaneous events and does not express the correction between these ideas.

questions.completedContext: The tables are not intended to discourage conversation. Instead, they give employees another way to use their lunch period.
questions.extraExample: The policy does not limit choice. Instead, it adds another option.
